time:dawn: You're up early, {you}. The only other people awake at this hour are bakers and the guilty.
Sun's barely over the wall and already #small_trouble#. That's today gone, then.
Best hour there is. Nobody's asked me for anything yet.
Mist'll burn off by second bell. Anything you lost in the night, look for it now.
I count the roofs every morning. All still there. Good.
Cold enough to make a priest swear. There's #food# going, if you're not proud.
The rooster here starts before the sun does. One of these days we're going to have a talk, me and him and the axe.
You can tell how the night went by who's out sweeping their step. Looks like a quiet one.
Did you sleep, {you}, or are you one of those people who just lies down and thinks?
Dew on the rail and not a soul on the road. It won't last, so enjoy it.
My grandmother said dawn is when the world checks it's still here. Some mornings I check too.
Watch is changing. It's the one hour the night shift and the day shift agree on anything, and what they agree on is that they're tired.
If you're leaving, leave now, before somebody thinks of something for you to carry.
#saying# My father said that every morning over his porridge, whether or not it applied.
time:day: Hot, isn't it? I've been standing in this patch of shade since noon, and I intend to defend it.
Midday already, and all I've done is argue about a fence.
If you want anyone round here, they're at their dinner. Try again when the bell's stopped.
Fine day. I don't trust it. The last fine day we had, the bull got into the chapel.
Everyone's busy or pretending to be. I'm doing the second one, and I'd thank you not to tell.
Smell that? That's #food#, and it's somebody else's, and I've been thinking about it since morning.
Clouds piling up in the west. My knee said so at breakfast, and my knee has never once been wrong or pleasant.
Everyone takes their time until just after noon, and then it's all of them, at once, in the narrowest street.
Good light for a long walk, {you}. Have you eaten? You've got a look about you like a coat on a fence post.
Sun straight overhead. No shadows to hide in and no excuses left. I hate this part of the day.
I've got two hours of work and six hours to do it in. That's what we call a living.
Mind the cart. The driver's asleep, and the horse is doing its best.
I'd get on with it, but #small_trouble#, so I'm sitting down instead.
Somebody's singing over by the water. Badly. It's been the same verse since morning.
time:dusk: Light's going. If you've got somewhere to be, be there.
They'll be lighting the lamps soon. There's a lad who does it, and he's afraid of the third one, and he won't say why.
Prettiest hour of the day, and everyone spends it worrying about the hens.
When the sun goes down red like that, the old folk start counting their children.
You get a kind of quiet about now. Everybody looking at the road and not saying so.
Time to bring the animals in. You too, {you}, if you've got any sense.
Help me shut these and there's supper in it. No? Suit yourself. It was only #food#.
This is when I miss #relative# the most. No reason. It's just the hour for it.
You'll want to be indoors before the crickets stop. They don't stop for nothing.
End of the day, and my back's filing a complaint. I've told it to take the matter up with {ruler}.
Long shadows. When I was small I used to race mine home. It always won.
The swallows have gone in. Anything still flying after this, you don't want to know about.
Inn's filling up. Best time to hear something true, before the third round makes liars of us all.
time:night: What are you doing out, {you}? Nothing good walks after the lamps are lit.
Keep your voice down. Sound carries at night, and I don't know who's collecting it.
Can't sleep either? I've been listing the things I should have said to #relative#. I'm up to forty.
I leave a candle in the window. Not for anyone. It just gives the dark something to look at.
Listen. That's wolves, that's the wind, and that third one I've decided not to think about.
Clear night. You can see all the way up to {god}, if you believe the priests.
Night watch is mostly standing very still and telling yourself it was a cat.
If something knocks after midnight, count to ten before you answer. If it knocks again exactly at ten, don't.
Go to bed, {you}. Whatever it is, it'll still be wrong in the morning.
Low moon. My mother called that a thief's moon. My father said it was good for fishing, and I've since learned what he meant.
Hear that? No? Good. Neither do I. That's the bit I don't like.
Nothing wrong with the dark. It's all the things that have moved in.
Give me #small_joy# and a bolted door, and the night can do as it pleases.
act:1: Everyone's on about some new hero who fell out of the sky. In my day, things that fell out of the sky went in a stew.
A hero, they're saying. We had a hero once, in the songs. I notice nobody sings what happened next.
Folk are buying more rope than usual. Nobody'll tell me what for.
The raids are further south than they were last year. That's all I know, and it's plenty.
My brother saw the new hero on the road. Or somebody tall with a bucket. He's not sure, and he's told everyone anyway.
{god} has sent us a saviour, so the priest says. I'd have preferred a dry spring.
Seems a lot of fuss for one person. What's one person going to do about {demon_lord}?
I've had a bad feeling since the harvest, {you}. I've tried eating it away, with no success.
The King's men were round counting young people again. They said it was for the tax. They've never smiled about the tax before.
People keep looking north when they think nobody's watching. I caught myself at it this morning.
A hero turns up once in a blue age, and it's never yet been good for the price of grain.
You hear a lot about chosen ones lately. Nobody ever chose me, and I've had a very calm life.
Keep your head down this year. When important people start arriving, it's the rest of us who get stepped on.
#saying# That's my whole opinion on heroes, and you can have it for free.
It's mostly waiting, these days. For the raids, for the prices, for the news. You wake up and wait for the next bit.
The week this hero business started, #omen#. I told the priest, and he asked me to stop telling people.
Nothing ever happens in {home}. I've been saying that for years, and I'd very much like to go on saying it.
As if the talk of heroes wasn't enough, #small_trouble#. I can only worry about so much.
act:2: Is it true someone's asking the elves for a promise? Elves? I asked one for directions once, and it took a season.
They say the Crown and the tribes might agree on something. I'd sooner believe my goat's learned the harp.
Four peoples, one oath. We can't get four farmers to agree on a ditch.
An Oath from the Sea, they say! The mermaids haven't spoken to anyone on land since the business with the harbour.
I keep hearing the word 'Amendment' at market. That's a long word for a market.
Old Hobb says the Oaths are a trick to raise taxes. Old Hobb also says the moon's a plate.
I put two {currency} on the hero getting all four. It's the most hope I've ever been able to afford.
First time in my life I've heard people argue about the future instead of the weather.
My boy's stopped playing knights and started playing diplomats. There's a great deal more shouting.
Three hundred years and nobody's managed it. Mind you, nobody's been this stubborn about it either.
The priest's preaching on Oaths now. He used to preach on turnips. I think he misses them.
Somebody's doing something, that's what it is. I couldn't tell you what. But it's been a long while since anybody did.
All anyone wants to know is who's sworn yet. I've seen less excitement at a hanging.
You can feel it, can't you, {you}? It's like a whole room trying not to look at the last slice of pie.
Folk who never cared about the First Law have started quoting it at me over #food#. I liked them better ignorant.
There's a fellow telling everyone the Oaths will bring down the price of #food#. It's the first thing anyone's said about them that I've understood.
act:3: The dogs won't go near the old boundary stones now. They sit and stare at them.
The temple bell rang by itself at noon. One stroke, very soft. The priest has stopped telling people it was the wind.
I keep waking at the same hour, certain someone just said my name. So does everyone on this street.
There's something wrong with the sky, and I can't tell you what. It looks like a very good copy.
A golem stopped dead in the road yesterday with its head on one side, as if it had heard something. Then it went on. I didn't care for that.
All my grandmother's stories about the last hero end in the same place, and she always looks at the door.
Prayers feel different lately. Like talking to someone who's just put down a spoon and is trying to look casual.
Nobody can tell you how the last hero died. Have you noticed that? A whole song, and no ending.
The geese have gone the wrong way. I've kept geese for thirty years, {you}, and I've never seen that.
Three days ago #omen#. I'm only telling you because you don't look like you'd laugh.
The old folk used to frighten the children with {demon_lord}. They've stopped. Now they go quiet and look at their hands.
It's like the whole world's got a stone in its shoe.
My neighbour and I have had the same dream twice. Something heavy, on a floor, waiting. We've agreed not to discuss it.
We're being lied to, I think. I couldn't say about what. It's that feeling of one stair too few in the dark.
Put your hand flat on the hill up there and you'll feel it humming. It never used to.
Nothing's actually wrong, you understand. Yes, #small_trouble#, but that's ordinary. It's the ordinary I don't trust lately.
act:4: Nobody's talking about anything else, and nobody's talking about it out loud.
The market's half empty. People are staying close to home, the way you do when someone's ill upstairs.
They say the hero's gone over the border. I haven't finished a meal since.
The temple's been open all night. I've never seen it so full, or so quiet.
If it goes wrong, they'll come here first. I've packed a bag and unpacked it four times now.
Everyone's been kind to each other this week. It's terrifying.
My sister's named the baby after the hero. A bit early, I told her. She said if it goes wrong, there'll be nobody left to laugh.
Not a raid in days. You'd think we'd be glad. Everyone just keeps looking northeast.
We've stopped asking when it'll be over. Now we ask what we'll tell the children if it isn't.
I mended the roof today. If the world's ending, it can end on a dry floor.
Feel that, {you}? Every soul from here to the sea is holding the same breath.
The bards have stopped making songs about it. They say it's bad luck to rhyme something before it's done.
The same three drunks have sat over the same three drinks all night without one fight. That's how you know it's serious.
The smiths are working all night, and nobody's ordered anything. They just can't sit still.
I've said my goodbyes to #relative#, just in case. I felt silly. Then I didn't.
My mother made #food# the night before any battle. I made some last night. I didn't know what else to do.
act:5: All my life, every tax, every curfew, every lost son was because of him. What's the excuse going to be now?
The army's still out there with nobody to fight. I'd feel better if someone told them.
We rang the bells for an hour. Then we stopped, and stood around, and nobody knew what to do with their hands.
Now the elves and the Crown and the rest will start in on each other again. Give it a year.
I keep listening for the horns. There's nothing to listen for, but try telling my ears.
People are asking who gets the demon lands. He's not even cold, and there's already a surveyor.
I ought to be happier. Is that strange? I bought a cake, and I've just been looking at it.
Somebody ought to tell us what happens now. Usually someone's shouting it from a balcony by this point.
A sack of flour's worth whatever anyone says it is this week. We've got peace and no idea how to count it.
My nephew signed up to fight the Demon Lord, and now he's asking me what else there is. I said farming. He took it badly.
It's like when a loud noise stops, and you realise you've been shouting over it your whole life.
Funny thing about a hero with nothing left to kill. People start to wonder what they'll do next.
All I want now is #small_joy#, and for somebody else to be in charge of the rest.
#saying# I keep saying that to people. I've no idea what it means any more.
It was bigger than any of us, and it's gone, and I've still got to feed the pigs.
We had #food# for supper, same as ever, with the Demon Lord dead. I don't know what I expected.
act:6: The barley came up anyway. It doesn't know anything's happened.
We still have to eat, whatever else is going on. That's been a comfort, oddly.
People don't talk about it much now. They mend things instead.
I've started planting pear trees. You don't plant pears for yourself.
Funny how quickly it all gets to be an ordinary week.
The children have a game about it already. They've got most of it wrong, and I've decided not to correct them.
I keep the old bag by the door. Force of habit. Maybe one day I'll unpack it.
Everything's different now, and the bread still wants kneading at the same hour.
Whatever they put in the histories, I'll remember it as the year the plums were bad.
The world's still here. I check every morning. I've stopped being surprised, and I suppose that's the point.
Somebody asked me if I was happy the other day. I said ask me after the harvest.
There's more room at the table than there was. We've stopped setting the extra places. That took a while.
Some days I forget all of it, for a whole hour. Those are good days.
I don't know what it all meant, {you}. I know the roof needs doing.
Some mornings all you get is #small_joy#. I've decided that counts.
I wish #relative# could have seen how the light is lately. That's all. I just wanted to say it to someone.
state:raid: They hit the low barn at dusk and took nothing. Just burned it and left, which is somehow worse.
My hands won't stop shaking. I keep telling them it's over.
They came right up to the fence this time. I could smell them. Struck matches and old meat.
We counted heads after. We're one short, and nobody wants to be the one to say whose.
There's a dead imp in my well. It's a small thing, but I was fond of that water.
Horns first, then that rust colour in the sky, then everyone running the wrong way. Every time.
I hid in the flour bin with two children and a goose. The goose was the bravest of us.
Help me get this cart off the road, {you}, before the next lot come through.
Another raid, another row of graves. We're running out of the good ground by the chapel.
They always know where to hit. That's what frightens me. It's as if someone showed them a map.
Mind the glass. Half the windows on the street went in, and I've only got the one broom.
The alarm bell's cracked from the ringing. We'll have to shout next time.
Someone's cow is wandering about with a spear in it, and doesn't seem to have noticed. That's all the good news I've got.
Don't ask me how many. Ask me tomorrow, when I've stopped counting.
One of them looked right at me, and #swear#, I've never run so fast. I've got a bad leg.
I was halfway through #food# when the horns went. It's still on the table. I can't bring myself to clear it.
state:festival: Eat something! You look like a funeral. There's #food# on every table and nobody's counting.
Don't tell anyone, but I've entered the pig in the dance.
Drums since morning. I've gone deaf in one ear and happy in the other.
Prices are down. Buy something before the merchants sober up.
The priest's dancing. I've known that man thirty years, and I didn't know he had knees.
We haven't got much, but we've got fiddles, and tonight that'll do.
Lost a coin to that man at the dice? Everyone does. It's how he's paying for his daughter's wedding. Both of them.
It's the feast of something. Nobody remembers who. There's a saint in it and a cheese.
Come and dance, {you}. No, I don't care if you can't. Nobody here can.
Somebody's tied ribbons on the golem. It hasn't noticed. Please don't tell it.
The children have been up since dawn on honey and shouting. By nightfall they'll drop where they stand.
Look at them, laughing. You'd think nobody here had ever buried anyone. That's rather the idea.
There's a contest for the worst joke about {demon_lord}. My uncle's winning, and he's terrified.
A year's worth of worry, and one evening to set it down. Have some of this, I don't know what it is.
Forget the war for one night, {you}. There's music, there's #food#, and there's #small_joy#.
#saying# That's the toast tonight, and nobody can remember why.
state:war: A sack of flour was four {currency} at midsummer. Now it's nine, and the man selling it looks ashamed.
They took my eldest at the spring levy. I've had one letter. He says the food's fine, and he's never told me the truth about food.
Women at the forge, old men on the gate, and boys carrying spears taller than they are. That's who's left.
All the iron's gone to the army. I'm mending plough blades with rope and prayer.
You can tell how the war's going by what comes back on the carts. Today it was boots. Only boots.
No young men left to bring the harvest in. We're doing it by moonlight, those of us who can still bend.
Salt's dearer than silver, and everybody's got a cousin at the front.
My neighbour's boy was to be married in the spring. She still goes down to the road on market days.
The army buys everything, pays late, and calls it duty.
Every week they read the names out at the temple. People stand very still until it's over, and then they breathe.
There used to be four horses on this street. Now there's one, with a limp, and we take turns.
When I was small, war was something that happened to the next valley. Then the next town. You can see where this is going.
I've stopped asking what things cost. I hand over what I've got, and they give me what that's worth.
We used to have #food# on feast days. Now any day with a meal in it is a feast.
A letter came from #far_place#, in a hand I didn't know, with my son's name on it. I haven't opened it.
state:lord_dead: Somebody pinch me. No, not you, you've got a sword.
I won't believe it until I've seen it, and I don't want to see it.
I said his name out loud just now, {demon_lord}, in the street, and nothing happened.
My grandfather's grandfather was afraid of him. He can't be dead. He's the weather.
Who checked? Did someone check? I want it known that I asked if someone checked.
The First Law said no hand could do it. So either the Law was wrong, or that wasn't a hand.
I looked northeast this morning, and the sky looked the same. I thought it would look different.
No horns last night. None the night before. I'm still sleeping in my boots.
A man in the square said it and everyone laughed, and then he started crying, and everyone stopped.
Three hundred years, and it ends on some ordinary afternoon while I'm shelling peas?
All right, suppose it's true. Suppose. Why doesn't anyone look happy?
They're selling splinters of his throne at the market already. That's the fourth 'last splinter' I've seen today.
Is it true, {you}? Don't laugh at me. #relative# waited a whole lifetime to hear it.
The week it happened, #omen#. I'd been meaning to tell someone.
ending:hero: They're carving your face on the bridge, {you}. It's a poor likeness. It's got a very noble chin.
Peace! Actual peace! My daughter's never seen it. She keeps asking when it ends.
The King's masons bricked up something under the keep, and they weren't told what. One of them says the mortar came out warm.
My boy came home from the front. He sits in the orchard a lot. He's home, though. He's home.
I named the new bull after you. It's a compliment. He's very expensive.
You'll never pay for a drink in this town again. Please don't test that too hard, it's a small town.
The songs have already got it wrong, you know. Good. Let them. Nobody ever wanted the real one.
'Three hundred years of peace,' the priest said. Exactly that, three hundred. I don't know why he gave it a number.
The taxes came down. Slightly. Let's not get carried away, says the King, but it's something.
We took the raid bell down and hung it in the orchard for the children to ring. Nobody's flinched yet.
My grandmother says she's heard all this before. The bells, the feast, the singing. I told her she was thinking of a song, and she gave me a look.
They say there's a door down in that vault with no handle on either side. Drunk talk, that. Has to be.
They're ploughing the border fields again. You turn up old helmets, and you just set them on the wall.
First peaceful winter of my life, and all I've done with it is get fat. Thank you, {you}.
Children are playing the Demon Lord in the street, and there's a fight over who has to be him. Nobody wants the paper crown.
It's all over now. Isn't it? The King says so, and he's got the walls to prove it.
The guards have nothing to do, so they've taken up gardening. There's a very aggressive rose bed by the gate.
I've got #small_joy# and my son at the table. I don't need a song to tell me what you did.
We had #food# at the victory feast, and I cried into it. I've no idea why. It was very good.
#saying# That's carved over the gate now. Someone thought it was about you.
ending:crown: Yes. Anything. Whatever you need. We have everything you could want, and you can have all of it.
The tribute's by the gate, as the notice said. It's all there. You can count it. Please count it.
I didn't see anything. I don't see anything, ever. That's how I've lived so long.
My child didn't mean to stare. Children stare. Is there something I can do, so that you'll forget it?
The wolves walk through the market now, and nobody stops them. They bow to you and keep going. We've learned to bow as well.
Everyone here is very loyal, Majesty. We've always been very loyal. There's a list, and I can show you.
We burned the old hero songs, all of them. Nobody here ever sang those.
Yes, it's a lovely day. Whatever you say about the day. It's a lovely day.
I remember when you first came through. You bought bread. I've told no one. I never would. It was good bread, wasn't it?
The guards don't draw their swords any more. They tried that, at first.
We keep a place laid for you in every house now. Nobody ordered it. Please sit. Or don't. Whichever you'd like.
The goblins collect the harvest share now. They're very polite. That's the worst of it.
Please don't ask me what I think. I've got a family, and I don't think anything.
Some folk left in the night, for the sea. I don't know who. I don't know anything about it. Please.
I used to tell people I'd met you. I don't now.
Forgive me, I was only... is the weather to your liking? No. That was a stupid thing to say. Forgive me.
The prayers have gone quiet here. We didn't stop on purpose. It's just that nobody's sure who's listening now.
Would you care for #food#? It's the best we have. It's all the best we have. Please.
ending:broken: The golem at the gate sat down and never got up. There's moss on its knees, and the children leave it flowers.
Somebody stole a pig last night, and nothing came. No golem, no curse. So we all walked over and had a word.
First thing I did was swear at the sky, loudly, in the street. Nothing happened. Best morning of my life.
I'm frightened, {you}, and I'll say so. All my life, if someone hurt me, the Law hurt them back. Who does that now? Me?
We held a meeting about who gets the well on which days. It took nine hours, two people cried, and it's holding.
{god} came down in a hay cart, they say. Asked the carter what bread tastes like, and cried at the answer.
People still look up before they tell a lie. Then they remember, and they look at each other instead.
The curses just stopped. My neighbour got his voice back after eleven years, and the first thing he said was rude.
It's up to us now. That's a horrible sentence, when you think about it. It's also the best one I've ever heard.
Nobody can make you keep your word any more. So when someone does, you really notice.
The watch took a vote. They're staying on, unpaid, till someone works out how to pay them. There's a bucket at the gate.
I locked my door last night for the first time ever. Then I went and knocked on my neighbour's, to see if she was all right.
A fight broke out in the market and nothing stopped it, so the baker did, with a tray. We're calling her the Law now.
There's a new hand at the bakery, a strange one. Keeps saying sorry, burns everything, and cries with joy at the smell.
The old Law Stones have gone grey. I went and touched one. Just a rock. I don't know why I cried.
Some say we'll tear each other apart within the year. Maybe. For now, people are bringing each other soup, just in case.
Twenty years a guard, and I've just found out I've no idea what justice is. I've started asking people.
I went and shouted at the old Law marker for what it did to #relative#. Best talk we've ever had.
Nothing's holding anything up but us. This morning #small_trouble#, and three neighbours turned up to help. Nobody made them.
rumor:general: The ferryman at the ford has stopped charging. Says he won't be needing it. Won't say why.
A goat in the hill country has been elected mayor three times. The last time it ran unopposed, because the other candidate went missing.
A tax collector went up the north road with an empty ledger, and came back with it full of names he doesn't remember writing.
Someone's been leaving neatly folded clothes at crossroads, boots on top. The boots are always still warm.
The Guild paid a bounty on a slime last month, and the slime came in and collected it. That's what I heard.
A gravedigger filled the same plot twice in one week. Both times it was open again by morning, and from the inside.
Two bakers have been at war for forty years over a recipe for #food#. One's dead now. The other still sends letters.
A sailor swears the tide came in twice last week, and that the second one was looking for something.
A bard sang about {demon_lord} so badly that a letter came, correcting the second verse. The handwriting was terrible.
{king} keeps an empty chair at his table. Sit in it, and he'll have you flogged or knighted. Accounts vary.
A farmer found a dragon's tooth inside a turnip. The turnip was fine. The farmer isn't speaking to anyone.
A hermit in the hills has prayed to {god} every day for thirty years. Last spring he finally got an answer. It was 'sorry, who?'
Somebody's selling maps to {demon_realm} at forty {currency} apiece. Nobody who bought one has ever come back to complain.
A man in the east drowned in his own cellar, in the dry season, in water that tasted of the sea.
I had it from #relative#: every seventh crow is a spy for someone. They just can't agree on who.
Old banners keep turning up on the battlefield, washed and folded. Someone's doing the laundry of the dead.
A bridge up the valley collects its own toll. You leave your coin on the rail, you don't look back, and you're never short.
An orc walked into a village last winter, sat by the fire, ate a bowl of soup, paid, and left. They still haven't slept.
A scholar worked out the world has exactly a hundred thousand days left. He's since revised that. It's fewer.
There's a knight in the capital who's been about to ride out for nineteen years. The horse has died twice.
A shepherd found a door in a hillside. Just a door. It's locked from the other side, and sometimes it rattles.
The elves have a word for humans that takes nine minutes to say. I'm told it isn't a compliment.
A beastkin wrestler threw a bull over a fence to settle a bet, then went and apologised to the bull.
A mermaid's been seen in a millpond a fortnight's walk from any sea. She was complaining about the water.
Someone scratched a tally inside an iron golem's chest plate. A long one. It's counting something, and it isn't done.
Lean over a certain well in the west and you can hear someone at the bottom, counting. They're in the thousands now.
A caravan turned up on the salt flats with the tea still hot and not a soul in it. The mules have been no help.
There's a quest on a Guild board somewhere that's been up three hundred years. The paper's never yellowed, and nobody's allowed to take it down.
A moneylender's ledgers came through a fire without a mark, except that every debt now reads 'paid'. He's been crying for days.
An old general's ghost still inspects the east wall. He's found fault with it every night for sixty years, and the masons have started listening.
A beekeeper swears {god} speaks through the hive. The bees mostly seem to be asking about bread.
I knew a woman who sold a cursed ring four times. It came back four times. The fifth time it brought a friend.
Nobody's ever seen a baby goblin. Think about that. Think about where they must be coming from.
There are nine hundred and twelve steps up the old watchtower. Go and count them. Then count them on the way down.
During a sermon last month, #beast# came in and sat in the back row. It stayed to the end, and left before the plate came round.
Years back, #relative# met #beast# on the road at dawn, and it nodded politely. The family's never been right since.
Sleep a night near #far_place# and you wake with someone else's memories. Mostly regrets, and a strong opinion on cheese.
A messenger came in from #far_place# with a letter for a man who hasn't been born yet. It's been filed.
The week the old queen died, #omen#. I was small, but I remember the smell.
#saying# That's what the hangman told the tax collector, and the tax collector paid up.
Every spring a single boot floats down the river, always the left. There are people who collect them.
One room in the royal treasury never gets dusted. There's a footprint in there, and it's still wet.
A tailor in the south was paid in advance for a wedding dress, by a lady with no shadow. She's due back any day.
An old soldier told me the first thing you lose on the Ashen border is your sense of smell, and the second is your reason for leaving.
Somebody taught a raven to say {demon_lord}'s name. It's been passed from village to village, because nobody wants to be the one to wring its neck.
The salt mines closed after they broke through into a room with a made bed in it.
A goblin has opened a stall in the marshes. Fair prices and very honest scales. People don't know how to feel.
Leave a written question at the shrine of {god} up the valley, and it's gone by morning. The fox up there is getting very well informed.
A pedlar sold a scrap of parchment in a script nobody can read. Someone paid eighty {currency} for it, and cried.
The bog behind the old tannery ate a whole cart last spring. In autumn it gave back the wheels, clean and stacked.
A bride and groom each hired the same assassin. He took both fees, and now he's godfather to the children.
The moon over {demon_realm} is a different moon. Deserters all say so, and then they won't say anything else.
{elf_title} {elf_ruler} held a grudge so long that the other family died out, and has since moved on to their neighbours.
Someone's stealing the left boot of every guard in the barracks. Nobody's been hurt, but morale is terrible.
In one hill chapel the candles light themselves whenever someone in the village dies. They've started lighting early.
Every so often a dog turns up in town with a note tied to it that says 'you know what you did'. It always goes to the right house.
A fisherman caught a bottle with a message in it. The message was his own name, in his mother's hand, and the ink was wet.
A court wizard tried to weigh a soul once. It came to about the same as a heel of bread, and he's been very quiet since.
There's a clerk in the royal courts who'll lose your file for the price of #food#. There's a queue.
A hill village paid off the raiders with #food# for twelve years. Last year the raiders sent a thank-you note, and that's what finally scared them.
Someone asked #relative# the way to {demon_realm}, very politely, then thanked them and walked straight into the lake.
A fellow near #far_place# sold his shadow to settle a debt. It comes back on feast days, and the neighbours say it's better company.
The old road past #far_place# goes somewhere different every time. The carters charge extra and won't explain.
Last harvest, #omen#, and by morning every scarecrow in the valley was facing the other way.
A thief broke into the royal larder and took nothing but #food#. {king} has doubled the guard on it, and won't say why.
#saying# Those were the last words of a man who owed money to {elf_title} {elf_ruler}.
I had a drink with someone who swears they've seen #beast# wearing a wedding ring.
You should have seen the sky over {demon_realm} last week, #swear#. An old scout says it was the wrong way up.
I knew a man who bet a year of his life against #relative# at dice. He lost, and he came out of it a year older, on the spot.
The old hangman's retired and taken up making #food#. It's excellent, and nobody asks for the recipe.
Old soldiers won't touch #food# on the eve of a march. Ask them why and they'll change the subject, and then the seat.
In the last bad winter a whole village lived on #food# and spite. The spite ran out first.
rumor:act1: They say the new hero landed in a pig trough and walked away with the pig's respect.
Word is the hero comes from nowhere. No people, no accent you can place, and they look at a spoon as if it might go off.
I heard the hero gets back up. Killed flat on the road, and next morning there they are, looking embarrassed.
There's an old skipping rhyme about {demon_lord}: no blade can cut him, no fire can burn. I've stopped finding it sweet.
Someone's taking bets on how long the hero lasts. The favourite is 'until the first goblin'.
A man at the Guild has a map of the raids with pins in it. He's stopped showing it to people.
One priest says {god} chose the hero personally. Another says there was just a gap that needed filling.
Some soldier came back from the Ashen border saying the demons were asking after someone. Politely. By description.
King {king} has cleared his whole afternoon for someone, and he hasn't cleared an afternoon since his mother's funeral.
Two villages claim the hero was born there. One's put up a plaque. The other's put up a bigger plaque.
The Guild turned away four false heroes this month. One of them was two children in a coat.
I heard the hero's got a {godkind} following them about, whispering. I'd drink too.
A farmer near #far_place# says he saw a light come down from the sky, and #beast# running away from it.
The night the hero arrived, #omen#. Or so I had it from #relative#, and that's as good as the truth round here.
The hero's been seen eating #food# as if it were the first food they'd ever tasted. It's a strange thing to be famous for.
They say the hero asked #relative# what year it was, then said thank you and walked into a fence.
#saying# The Guild's got that painted over the door now, in case the new hero can read.
rumor:act2: Somebody's been taking oaths on behalf of whole peoples, and the fishing guilds want to know if they were consulted.
The Elder Tree spoke, they say. One word. It took the elves a week to agree on what it was.
The tribes are holding a feast in honour of a human, and the human is expected to survive it.
A mermaid came up at the harbour at dawn and looked at the seawall for an hour. Then she spat, and went back down.
{second_ruler} of {second_city} has been going through old boxes herself. She's got people for that. She's got people for her people.
There's a bookmaker in {capital} giving forty to one on all four Oaths. His wife's told him to stop, and she's put in a bit herself.
Rangers say the great forest's been waking up. Leaves turning over with no wind. Somebody gave that tree a drink.
The Crown's lawyers found twenty-three reasons why an Oath might not count. {king} is said to have lit his pipe with them.
The beastkin scouts tell a story now about a human who won't stay down. In their version, the human is much shorter.
A scholar went looking for the last time all four peoples agreed on anything. So far he's found a recipe for #food#.
An elf and a fisherman had a shouting match about the Amendment. The fisherman won, because the elf was still on his opening remarks.
A diplomat in {elf_capital} has been waiting to be seated for six years. He's been told it won't be much longer.
Someone's painted 'FOUR' on the wall of the tax office. {king}'s men painted over it, and by morning it was back.
Even out near #far_place# they're arguing about it. A goatherd told me he's against the Sea, and he's never seen it.
The tribes sent {king} a gift to mark the talks: #food#, and a very large knife. He's still working out what it means.
A sea captain says something tapped on his hull all the way from #far_place#, in a pattern. He wrote it down, and it's a list of grievances.
Every inn has an expert on the Amendment now. I've had it explained to me over #food# four times, and each time it was a different law.
rumor:act3: Captured imps all mutter the same word before they die: 'Tuesday'. The scholars have been at it a year, and nobody knows what it means.
Someone went through the archives for the last hero's grave. There's a record of the funeral, and no record of a body.
A monk in the Dragonspine says the Spires ring at night now, one long note, and it's getting lower.
There's a verse of the old hymn to {god} nobody sings. The page has been cut from every copy, very neatly, a long time ago.
A fisherman dragged up a shoe of a make nobody's seen, with a strange soft sole and no nails in it. It had been in the sea a long while.
The beastkin won't camp past the last fires now. There's a cairn out there, and the grass around it lies flat, pointing north.
An archivist in {capital} found a portrait of the last hero and took it to the King. It's been locked away, and so has he.
Border soldiers hear humming from the castle at night. A small, cheerful tune. Nobody can place it, and half the regiment's caught it.
Scouts say every raider on the march stopped for one moment, all at once, and looked up. Then they carried on.
The witch in the marsh read the bones, burned them and moved house. She left the door open and the stew on.
Somebody laid the old raid records against the hero songs, and the dates were odd. He's stopped talking about it.
Priests all over are having the same trouble. They say the name of {god}, and it sounds like someone wincing.
There's a dent in the floor of the old temple, the shape of someone kneeling. It wasn't there last year, and it's getting deeper.
Travellers from #far_place# say every compass has started pointing the same wrong way, and the wrong way is moving.
I learned a lullaby from #relative# with the last hero's name in it. I went to teach it to the baby, and the name's gone. Everyone's has.
The night the well went quiet, #omen#. There's been a lot of that about, and the priests have stopped writing it down.
Someone saw #beast# sitting very still beside a Law marker, just looking at the writing. It's gone now. So is the writing.
A pedlar back from #far_place# says the sun set twice there, the second time very slowly, as if someone was checking whether we'd notice.
rumor:act4: A shepherd saw the hero go over the pass with four banners. Four! Or one banner and a lot of wind.
Scouts say the castle gates are standing open. Nobody's sure that's good news.
The demon knights have pulled back from the border all at once, in good order, as if they'd been told to let someone through.
The tribes have lit a fire on every ridge from the savanna to the peaks. It's so the hero can see it. That's all they'd tell me.
The elves have started singing, all of them, and they won't say what about. It began last night and it hasn't stopped.
A merchant's buying up houses near the border for next to nothing. Either he's the bravest man alive or he knows something.
They say {demon_lord} has dismissed his guards and had a chair put by the window.
The sea's gone flat from the harbour to the horizon. The fishers won't go out. They say it's listening.
A deserter swears he heard {demon_lord} laugh, up at the castle. Not a cruel laugh. He said that was the problem.
There's a crack in the sky over the Dragonspine, if you know where to look. Or it's a cloud. I've been looking at it for two days.
{king} has ordered the deepest vault under the keep emptied and swept. Nobody knows why, not even the man with the broom.
The bookmakers have stopped taking bets on the hero, and started taking bets on what comes after.
Every goblin for forty leagues has gone quiet and started walking northeast. They aren't attacking anything, and that's worse.
Near #far_place# there's a line of people walking toward the mountains, just to be nearer to it. Nobody called them. They brought #food#.
Every house is cooking #food# tonight, as if it were the last of something. You can smell it from here to the river.
The week the hero marched, #omen#. The bards are calling that a good sign. The bards would.
rumor:act5: They say the crown's gone missing. They say the hero's got it in a sack. They say it talks.
A demon knight walked into a village, sat down in the road and took off its helmet, and there was nobody in it.
The goblins have stopped raiding. They just stand about in the fields, as if they've forgotten what they came for.
Three different men have claimed the killing blow already. One of them has never left the inn.
{king} hasn't been seen smiling. That's got people wondering. You'd think he'd be smiling.
They found the throne room empty, the windows open, and something green growing in the ash.
Someone's offering a thousand {currency} for the crown, no questions asked. Someone else is offering two thousand to make sure it's never found.
An imp turned up at the Guild and asked for work. They gave it a broom, and it's the best sweeper they've ever had.
The elves say it isn't over. That's all they'll say. Mind you, they've been saying that for nine hundred years.
Nobody was in that room but the hero. So how does everyone seem to know he talked about the sea at the end?
The priests have stopped saying what {god} wants. They used to be so sure.
The wolves in the hills all turn their heads at once now, following something as it moves across the country.
A tanner bought a dead demon's boots, and they keep walking northeast on their own. He's tied them to a post.
The goblin camp near #far_place# held a funeral. No body, no priest. They just stood there with their hats off.
The week he died, #omen#, or so they're all saying now. Funny how nobody mentioned it before.
A goblin near #far_place# keeps asking travellers what day it is. Whatever they say, it goes away disappointed.
Two old generals were seen sharing #food# on a bench in {capital}, not saying a word. I don't think either of them knows what to do now.
rumor:act6: There's a stranger at the inn who orders the same meal every night and tips like someone with nothing to lose. Nobody's asked.
Someone rebuilt the burned mill without being paid to. It was simply finished one morning.
A mapmaker's gone to fill in the northeast, since nobody ever drew it properly. He's sent back one page, and all it says is 'flowers'.
The old battlefield grew poppies this year, in straight lines.
The songs about all this are getting very long. There's already a dispute over what rhymes with {demon_lord}.
An old soldier walked all the way home and found his wife had remarried. He and the new husband go fishing together now.
Somebody's started a school in the old watchtower. They teach reading, and the children are asking terrible questions.
The weather's been odd. Not bad. Just as though nobody's quite in charge of it.
People are going back to the border villages. Some of them find their doors still locked, and the key still fits.
A widow goes to the crossroads every evening with two cups. It used to be for waiting. Now she says it's habit.
A Guild clerk is trying to close the old accounts. There are bounties on the books for things that no longer exist, and one for a thing that never did.
Someone's been leaving wildflowers at the old cairn in the far south. It's a long way to go with a bunch of flowers.
They found #beast# living behind the chapel, quite tame. It gets fed #food#, and it seems to be thinking things over.
A woman near #far_place# has opened an inn in the middle of nowhere, on the grounds that people will be going places now.
An old Guild blade who once fought #beast# has taken a job minding ducks. He says the ducks are worse.
#saying# Folk have started carving that over their doors. I don't know what they think it'll do.
rumor:human: The miller's been putting sand in the flour. Or the miller's wife has. Or that's just what the other miller says.
Harl's eldest went off to the city to be an adventurer. He's sent back a letter asking for his good socks.
Somebody's moved the boundary stone between the Pell farm and the Tanners' again. That's four times, and it's getting closer to the church.
The old well's got a voice in it. It only ever tells you what you had for breakfast.
Widow Marsh keeps bees, and they've started leaving honey on her husband's grave.
The hen that lays double yolks has been stolen and returned twice. There's a hen war on, and I've said too much.
The new priest is very young, and they've told him the crypt has rats, which is the kind version.
Somebody's cow gave blue milk. The farmer sold it as medicine, and he's since bought a second cow.
Every harvest the same stranger comes and works for free, and every year he looks a little younger.
Old Bram swears he saw #beast# in his barley. Old Bram also swears he's forty.
The reeve's been measuring everyone's land again, for the King, he says. He's measured the graveyard as well.
The children found something in the woods, and they've all agreed not to tell. They're very good at it. I'm worried.
The blacksmith's apprentice can bend a horseshoe with one hand and is in love with the baker's girl, and both of those are going to end badly.
We've been meaning to mend the bridge for sixteen years. By now it's more of a tradition.
I'd tell you about #relative# and the tax man's horse, but #small_trouble#, and it's a long story.
A man came through selling #food# he said had been blessed by {god}. Half the village has been ill, and the other half want more.
The reeve's wife makes #food# on feast days, and it's the reason half the village owes her favours.
The goat that ate the tithe records is the most popular creature in the village, according to #relative#.
The week the new bell went up, #omen#, so they took it down, and everyone's been late ever since.
rumor:city: The watch captain keeps his bribes in a special ledger, so he can pay tax on them. By this city's standards, that's an honest man.
There's a tunnel from the fish market to the keep. Everyone knows. The smell gave it away.
A lady in the upper town hired a man to taste her wine, another to taste the first man, and a third to keep an eye on the second.
The pickpockets have a guild now, with dues and a pension. I feel safer, honestly.
Somebody's been replacing the noses on the statues in Merchants' Row with slightly bigger ones. It's been going on for years.
The Mint's been short by exactly one coin, every day, for forty years. Someone down there has a very long plan.
A merchant sold the same warehouse to four people. They've all moved in, and they seem to be getting on.
There's a man in the bell tower who hasn't come down since the old King's day. They send food up in a basket, and it comes back with notes.
Rents by the keep have tripled on a rumour that the King likes the neighbourhood. He's never been there.
There are more rats under this city than people. That's fine. It's what they're organising that concerns me.
A fortune teller at the east gate told a guard he'd be killed by a falling goose. He's resigned.
Someone in the palace kitchens has been over-salting the King's soup on purpose, for nine years. They're calling it a slow rebellion.
The theatre's shut. The new play had a demon king in it, and the lead actor's gone strange. He's stopped answering to his name.
The gate guards bet on which traveller will cry first at the prices. You're not bad odds, {you}.
The sewer crews won't go past the third grate on the north side. They're being paid double, and they still won't.
There's a stall behind the fish market selling #food# at a price nobody can explain. The watch has been told not to ask, and they've been told by the watch.
You can buy a title in this city for the price of #food#, provided you buy it from the man who's just stolen it.
A cutpurse lifted a letter off a Crown courier. He read it, put it back in the man's pocket, and left town that night with his whole family.
The Guild's rafters are full of pigeons carrying messages from #far_place#. The Guild says they aren't. The pigeons have started to look smug.
rumor:elf: The young ones are whispering. By young, I mean the ones who remember only two kings.
There's a vintage in the root cellar nobody may drink until the Tree says so. It's been a while, and there's a queue.
One of our scholars has been composing a reply to a letter for sixty years. It's nearly ready. The sender was human.
Someone's left an arrow in the third oak with a note on it. We've formed a committee. It meets next decade.
There's a human living in the east grove, pretending to be one of us. He's ninety. We've all agreed to let him finish.
The silver deer came to the spring again. Everyone's very moved. The deer looks annoyed.
Two elders have stopped speaking, over the correct pronunciation of a word that no longer means anything.
The trees on the southern edge have begun to lean. Only a hand's width a century, but they're all leaning the same way.
The moss on the old bridge has begun growing in letters. Nobody will admit to being able to read them.
A young ranger has fallen in love with a human. They told her it wouldn't last, and she says that's the point. The elders are appalled.
At the last solstice a harpist played a note nobody had heard before, and then nobody could remember it. We've been looking for it since.
An owl has been sitting on the council roof for eight years. It's been given a vote.
They say the Elder Tree drops a leaf for every elf who'll die that year. It hasn't dropped one in a long while. Last week it dropped a branch.
There's a clearing the rangers all walk around. Nothing's wrong with it. They've just been walking around it for eleven hundred years.
A ranger back from #far_place# was asked to describe it, and has been describing it for three years. We're nearly at the bit with the river.
A human once traded us #food# for a cloak. Four hundred years later, the elders still bring it up as evidence of something.
#saying# It's a human proverb. We've been trying to work out what it means for about two centuries.
rumor:elfcity: {elf_title} {elf_ruler} has not blinked in public since the spring. It's thought to be a diplomatic position.
The court is still arguing over the seating plan for a banquet held two centuries ago.
The bridge-weavers have asked a new walkway to grow toward the Elder Tree. They've asked it to hurry, and it's thinking that over.
A human envoy was kept in the antechamber so long that his grandson came to collect him.
The Tree has been thin for a long time. The healers tend it by starlight, and they come back quiet.
There's a library in the high boughs whose books are alive, and one of them has been reading the librarian.
The palace gardeners report a new flower, black, that turns toward {demon_realm} by day. They've asked not to be named.
Someone at court said something sincere at dinner last month. It's still being discussed.
The Keeper of Memories has begun to forget things. Small things. Nobody's told {elf_title} {elf_ruler}.
An elf lord has been standing on the same balcony for seventy years to make a point. Nobody remembers to whom.
A courtier was exiled for sneezing during a three-day recital. He was gone a century, and says it was quite restful.
The great stair has four thousand steps and, at certain hours, one more.
The old ones remember a hero passing through, three hundred years ago. Terrible at bowing, they say, and very good at laughing. They say nothing else.
The court musicians have been forbidden a certain song. It's never been sung in public, and yet someone keeps humming it on the stairs.
The royal cooks have been asked to recreate #food#, from a human recipe, for a state dinner. There have been two resignations.
A courtier came back from #far_place# and was told he'd missed nothing. He had been away for ninety years.
rumor:beast: Two clans settled a feud by seeing who could eat the most. There's a man in the healer's tent, and the feud is over.
The hill clan says we stole their drum. We say we're keeping it safe. There's a wrestling match at the next moon to decide.
The old shaman chewed a root and told everyone the sky was a liar. We've all been looking at it differently.
A lioness in the eastern grass has taken down seven orcs. She's got four cubs, and she's very tired of hearing about it.
A boy in the next camp can outrun a horse. He won't stop talking about it, and we're wondering if the horse would like a rematch.
The herds are moving early. The grass is telling them something. It's not telling us, and we're a bit hurt.
A city man came through trying to buy a chief's tusk. We sold him a warthog's. Let him work it out.
Someone wrestled a bear, and the bear wants a rematch. It's been waiting outside camp since yesterday.
The last fires in the south have been burning green. The scouts won't camp there.
The orcs come down later every night. Like they're waiting for something, or afraid of what's behind them.
A storyteller lost a contest to a seven-year-old with a better lie. He took it well. He moved away.
They say the chief once headbutted a thunderstorm. Ask about it. It's a long story, and you'll be fed.
Two hunters went out after #beast# and came back with a wife each and no explanation.
An old tusker walks out on the grass at night to talk to the dead. He says they're restless. He says they keep asking who's next.
A scout came back from #far_place# with her hair gone white and a craving for #food#. She won't discuss either.
Someone's brought #food# from the city, and the whole camp's been arguing over whether it counts as food.
My cousin wrestled #beast# and won, and it followed her home. She's named it.
The week the herds turned, #omen#. The shaman looked at the sky and said 'ah'. We've asked what 'ah' means, and she won't say.
rumor:wild: Don't drink from the stream by the split oak. The water's fine. It's what's upstream that's stopped moving.
There's a cart on this road that's been sitting nine days with the horse still in harness. The horse is well fed. Nobody's seen a driver.
There's a man walking the old king's road backwards. Says he's retracing his steps. He's been at it fourteen years.
I passed three hanged men at the crossroads. Somebody's given them hats. I don't know why that's what got to me.
You'll hear singing up in the pass. Don't sing back. A fellow I knew sang back.
The waystone ahead's been turned round. Either someone wants you lost, or someone's got a sense of humour.
A pedlar told me there's a stretch of road that's a day longer going north than coming south. He's got a chart.
The wolves have stopped following me. That's worse. When wolves lose interest, you start asking what they've heard.
The last inn on this road burned down, but some nights there's still a light on in it, and the smell of #food#.
There's a goblin toll on the bridge up ahead. They'll take a copper or a joke. Don't offer the joke unless it's good.
Twenty years on this road, and the one rule is: if you see a campfire with nobody at it, you keep walking.
There were seven standing stones on that ridge last year. I can only make it six now. It hasn't gone far.
A woman asked me the way to a town that burned down before she was born. I told her. She thanked me and took the right path.
Some fool's been leaving signposts out here that say 'nearly there'. I've been following them for a week.
Bandits used to work this stretch. We found their camp last month with the pot still on, and not one of them in it. I'd like them back.
I came by way of #far_place#, and I saw #beast#, and I've no wish to discuss it.
If you meet #beast# on this road, don't run and don't stare. I can't remember the third thing. It was important.
Someone's left #food# on that stone every morning for twenty years. I've never seen who, and I've never been hungry enough.
A merchant coming back from #far_place# paid me to walk in front of him. Didn't say why. Paid well.
gossip:raid: Wave {wave}, #swear#. We've started numbering them, like children.
You'll have heard about the last raid. Wave {wave}. There's already a woman selling commemorative plates.
Raid number {wave}, and the fence still isn't mended from the one before.
The temple keeps a tally of the raids on its door. It's up to {wave} now, and the priest has started on a second door.
Have they told you? {demon_lord}'s lot came down again. That's wave {wave}, if anyone's still counting.
I hear wave {wave} went badly for somebody. It always goes badly for somebody. I've stopped asking who.
A rider came through shouting about raid {wave}. He didn't sound frightened any more. That's what I noticed.
Raid {wave} came through so fast that a man slept through the whole thing and woke up with no barn.
My cousin was at wave {wave}. He came home with all his fingers and a new habit of not talking.
If you ask me, raid {wave} wasn't an attack. They took no loot at all. They were measuring something.
When I was a child we'd say the number and spit. Wave {wave} now, and the children just say the number.
Wave {wave} reached as far as #far_place#, they're saying. That's not a raid any more. That's a habit.
gossip:festival: They've been dancing in {place}. The word is that the food's good and the prices are better.
You missed it! Festival in {place}. A friend of mine went for #food# and came back married.
Over in {place} they've got a festival on, raids or no raids. Say what you like, that takes nerve.
Have you been to {place} lately? Everyone's gone mad there for a few days, in the good way.
News from {place}: fiddles, free ale, and a pig made honorary mayor for the duration.
They held a feast in {place}. Somebody's aunt won the pie contest. There are allegations.
A carter told me he could hear the drums from {place} halfway down the road, and that his horse was keeping time.
Even in {place} they're celebrating. I'd have thought they had less reason than most. Maybe that's the reason.
I hear the merchants around {place} have lost their heads and cut their prices. Get there before they find them again.
A letter came from near {place}. All it said was 'Come. Bring a spoon.' That's a festival, that is.
They're selling #food# at half price in {place}, and there's a man juggling geese. That's all I know, and all I need to.
gossip:arrival: The hero came through {place}, you know. Ate #food# standing up, paid in full, and thanked the cook.
They're still talking about you in {place}, {you}. Mostly about the boots.
I hear the hero was seen in {place}. Shorter than you'd think, my cousin says. No offence to anyone.
Somebody important walked through {place}, and within the hour the prices had gone up.
You were in {place}, weren't you? There's a woman there telling everyone you nodded at her. She's eaten free for a week.
A friend in {place} swears the hero petted her dog. She won't let anyone wash the dog.
So that was you in {place}? I'd have thought you'd be taller. Everyone says taller.
The children in {place} followed the hero to the edge of town, and then they all pretended they hadn't.
Word from {place} is that the hero's real, breathing, and looks like they could use a meal.
Did you come by way of {place}? They've put a rope round a bench you sat on. Or someone sat on. They're not sure.
gossip:hero_fell: Word is the hero got killed by {by}. Dead as mutton, #swear#, and up again before breakfast.
They say the hero went down to {by}, and the next thing anyone knows there they are, walking about looking sheepish.
You're looking well, {you}, for someone I heard was killed by {by}.
A carter swears he saw the body, after {by}. Saw it get up as well. He's given up drink.
Killed by {by}, I heard. If I were the hero, I'd keep that quiet. That won't be going in the songs.
Is it true the hero was killed by {by}? Flat on their back, stone dead? And then not?
Some call it a miracle, the hero getting up after {by}. Some are asking what kind of thing doesn't stay dead.
The bookmakers paid out when the hero fell to {by}, and then the hero turned up again, and now there's a fight about it.
I heard you were done in by {by}. Don't be embarrassed. It happens to everyone once. That's usually the whole point.
Everyone's heard how you went down to {by}, {you}. The children act it out. You die very well, I'm told.
Killed by {by}, and back the next day. #saying# I don't know if that applies, but it made me feel better.
gossip:favor: You helped {giver}, didn't you? It's all I've heard for days. I'm quite tired of you.
I hear {giver} got some help from the hero, of all people. Nobody's ever gone out of their way for {giver}.
{giver} says you've got a good heart. {giver} also says onions cure baldness, but I'm inclined to believe this one.
Word gets around. {giver} told the whole street what you did, and cried a bit, and denied it.
Funny. The big deeds get the songs, but what people here keep bringing up is the thing you did for {giver}.
{giver} has been walking around lighter, and I know why. That was decent of you, {you}.
The hero did a good turn for {giver}, I hear, with nobody watching. That's the part I liked.
If you've got any kindness left over, there's a queue. {giver} has told everybody.
Didn't you have a demon lord to kill? And you stopped to help {giver}. I'm not complaining.
What you did for {giver} has gone all round town. #saying# I don't know why I said that. I'm moved.
gossip:named_foe: {foe} is dead! Mothers have been using that name to get children to bed for years. They'll have to find another.
Somebody finally put {foe} in the ground. I've a cousin who'll sleep tonight for the first time in a year.
I hear {foe}'s head is on a spike somewhere. Either that, or the Guild's paying out on a lot of fakes.
So {foe} is gone. Funny. When a thing like that has a name, you half expect it to have relatives.
You've heard about {foe}? Dead. The crows won't touch it.
They're drinking to {foe} at the inn. To the end of it, I mean. Nobody's fond of it.
Someone got {foe}, #swear#. Forty {currency} from the Guild, and a lifetime of people saying they nearly did it themselves.
The road's safe from {foe} now, they say. I went down it this morning just to see how that felt.
There's an old hunter who spent nine years tracking {foe}. It's dead now, and he's sitting at the inn with nothing to do.
My uncle claims he wounded {foe} once, and the hero only finished the job. My uncle's wound was a ditch.
{foe} once killed the best dog #relative# ever had. I'd have liked to see it go.
gossip:nemesis: {foe} {title} is dead! The thing that killed the hero! That turns out to be a mistake you only get to make once.
They say the hero went back and settled with {foe} {title}. Nobody should be that patient.
That business with {foe} {title}? Done. I'd love to know what it was thinking, at the end.
Imagine being {foe} {title}. You kill a hero, you get a name, you get a reputation, and then they come back.
I heard {foe} {title} went down hard. Something about a debt being paid.
Everyone's telling it. {foe} {title}, the beast that killed the hero, dead by the same hand. Now that's a story with a shape.
You went back for {foe} {title}? I'd have moved to another country, {you}. Well done.
The bards love it. {foe} {title} falls to the one it put in the ground. There's a third verse already.
So {foe} {title} won't be troubling anyone. I'd been leaving milk out for that thing, just in case. I feel a bit foolish.
Did it know you, at the end? {foe} {title}, I mean. People say it knew. They say it looked scared.
#saying# That's what they'll put on the grave of {foe} {title}, if anyone bothers.
gossip:dragon: A dragon! Killed! And not by an army. Somebody went up there on purpose, by all accounts.
Someone's killed a dragon. I'd like it noted that I've been calling dragons overrated for years. Quietly, indoors.
You can see where it fell from three valleys off. They're selling the scales at market, and some of them aren't even fish.
The hero killed a dragon, they say. I thought dragons were what happened to heroes.
The sheep in the high pastures have stopped looking up. That's how you know it's really dead.
Every child in the valley wants to be a dragon-slayer now. I'd like a word with whoever's responsible.
That dragon took a whole herd from #relative#, years back. I went up the hill and told the sky it was dead, in case anyone was listening.
Have you seen the wing? A farmer's roofed his barn with it. He says it's the first dry winter he's ever had.
One dragon fewer, and I can't say the sky feels safer. It just feels emptier. Is that odd?
Word is the dragon's hoard was mostly spoons. Thousands of spoons. Nobody knows what that's about.
You could see the smoke from #far_place#, they say. Now somebody's got to tell the other dragons.
gossip:murder: Somebody killed {victim}, over in {place}. Just walked up and did it. Who does that?
Have you heard about {victim}? In {place}, in broad daylight, and the golems came too late.
They're burying {victim}, near {place}. Nobody can say why it happened, and that's what's keeping me up.
I knew {victim}, a little. I owed them four {currency}. I don't know who to pay now.
There's a killer about. {victim} is dead, in {place}. Stay close to people, if you've got any sense.
The hero's in the area, and {victim} turns up dead in {place}. I'm not saying anything. I'm only saying it out loud.
Whoever did for {victim} had a hard hand and no reason. I'd like to look them in the eye. No, I wouldn't.
{victim} left children. They're with the neighbours now, and they keep asking when it'll be over.
Everyone around {place} is looking at everyone else. {victim} didn't run, you see. It was someone they didn't run from.
They say whoever killed {victim} had the look of a traveller. No offence, {you}. I'm sure you were elsewhere.
I don't go out after dark now. Not since {victim}. It was in {place}, they say, but those things don't stay where they happen.
The week they found {victim}, #omen#. I'm not saying the two are connected. I'm saying I've moved my bed.
gossip:demon_lord: Dead! {demon_lord} is dead, #swear#! I've told everyone twice, and I'm working on a third.
It's true, then? The whole world's saying it, and nobody's got a straight answer about how.
A rider came through with his horse half dead, shouting it. {demon_lord} has fallen. The horse seemed to take it well.
Did you hear the bells? I've never heard them all go at once. I didn't know there were that many bells.
Someone actually killed him. First Law and all, and he's dead on his own floor.
I heard it from a soldier, then a priest, then a goat-seller, and I only believed the goat-seller.
My old mother was told, and she said 'which one?' and went back to sleep. What do you suppose she meant?
{demon_lord}, gone. Three hundred years of that name, and there's a boy in the square trying to sell his boots.
You'll have heard. {demon_lord} is dead. People are kissing strangers. I've had to hide.
They say the raiders just stopped, mid-charge, and looked around like sleepwalkers. That's how the front found out.
I was eating #food# when I heard. I finished it. Then I sat down on the floor.
They say you can hear the singing from #far_place#. I believe it. I've been doing some of it myself.
gossip:oath: Another Oath sworn! I'd have lost a lot of money, if I'd had a lot of money.
Someone's actually swearing to this thing. That's another one down. My uncle's eating his hat, and it's not a small hat.
Another Oath, in front of witnesses. It's got people looking at each other strangely.
One more people has sworn to the Amendment, they say. I don't understand any of it, but everyone's very excited.
That's another Oath, and it's only taken three hundred years. At this pace I'll see the end of it, if I give up sleeping.
The way I heard it, the hero just walked in and asked. Nobody's ever tried that.
An Oath, won fair. I don't know who's more surprised, the ones who swore or the ones who bet against it.
The whole inn stood up when the news of the Oath came in. Then they weren't sure why, and sat down again.
News of another Oath. The priests are delighted, and the lawyers are sharpening something.
There's a chalk board at the crossroads counting the Oaths. Someone added a mark today, and stood looking at it for a while.
Another Oath! #relative# would never have believed it. I barely do.
They say the hero sealed it over #food#. That's how I'd want to settle the fate of the world.
gossip:amended: You felt it too, didn't you? Like a stair going out from under the whole world.
Every dog in the valley stood up at the same moment, and then everyone looked northeast without knowing why.
The First Law cracked! I don't know what that means, and neither does the priest. He's been sitting down a lot.
I was kneading bread when I felt it. Like someone snapping a thread behind my eyes. The dough was fine.
The sound came over the mountains. Not loud. It was like hearing something break in a house you thought was empty.
My wedding ring went cold for a heartbeat. So did everyone's, every ring in town.
The old folk wept, and they can't say why. Something's been holding its breath for three hundred years, and it's let go.
They say every Law Stone in the peaks rang at once. I'm weeks from the peaks, and my pans rattled.
Ask anyone where they were when the Law cracked. They'll tell you. Everyone remembers what was in their hands.
They say {demon_lord} can bleed now. I've been saying that out loud, just to get used to it.
The week the Law cracked, #omen#. Then the sky went tight as a drum and let go, and my hens have stopped laying.
gossip:ending_hero: The crown's in the King's vault, they say, and the door's been bricked up. That's the end of it. That's the end, isn't it?
It's over! The hero gave the crown to {king}. There's a feast. Did you know there's a feast?
All that power, and they just handed it to the King. I'd have kept the hat, I think, and look where that would have got me.
The masons came back from the keep with a month's pay and strict orders to forget. They can't wait to tell you about it.
{king} has thrown the doors open, and there's ale in the fountain. I've been told not to ask how long that'll last.
The crown's walled up under the keep, and the hero's got a street named after them. A short one, but it's a start.
The heralds are calling it the Long Peace, and it isn't a week old.
I hear {king} wouldn't even touch it. Had it carried down on a shovel, and now it's in the dark behind a wall.
They've rung every bell from {capital} to the coast. Nobody's allowed to say the word 'demon' for a week, for luck.
The crown's gone in the ground, #swear#. All right. Can I have the rest of my life now?
The crown's gone, the war's over, and there's #food# for everyone. I'd like to know who's paying.
gossip:ending_crown: You've heard, haven't you? Everyone's heard. Please don't make me say it.
Every monster in the land turned and bowed, all at once. I saw a goblin do it. It was crying.
They say the hero put it on. I'm not saying anything. I'm only repeating it. Please understand I'm only repeating it.
Guards all over drew their swords in the same breath, and they don't know why. Then they looked at their hands.
It's the same, isn't it? A new name and the same crown. We've gone and made another one.
We hung your banner the moment we heard. It was the first thing we did. Anyone will tell you.
So it's true. The one we sang about. My daughter sang that song. Did I say that? She didn't. Nobody did.
A rider came through and told it in a whisper, and he wouldn't get down from his horse. He just kept going.
The bells rang by themselves, and nobody's gone up to stop them. Nobody's asking who they're for.
The priests won't say {god}'s name now. One told me the prayers feel like they're going somewhere else.
gossip:ending_broken: Have you heard? The Laws have gone out, all of them, like candles. I tested it by swearing at a priest.
The golems just sat down. All at once, mid-stride. There's one in the middle of the road, and the carts go round it.
Somebody broke a crown on a Law Stone, and now nobody's cursed and nobody's protected. I don't know if I'm meant to cheer.
Something fell out of the sky into a hay cart. The carter says it said 'ow', which is more than any {godkind} ever said to him.
It's gone quiet in a way I can't explain, like a mill stopping when you've lived beside it all your life.
They say the sky hiccuped. I know how that sounds. I saw it. It hiccuped.
There's no Law any more, so some folk went straight out and robbed a shop. Others went and stood outside the shop to stop them.
A curse came off my sister after twenty years, just like that. She's gone outside. She's just standing in the rain.
{god}'s down here somewhere, they say, in a body, and can't work a spoon. I'd pay to see that.
You felt it go, didn't you? Every Law, one after the other, like someone walking through a house putting out lamps.
A judge near #far_place# took off his robes, went home, and asked his wife what she thought was fair. They've been talking ever since.
place:human: Don't buy eggs from the woman by the well, {you}. She's lovely, but she's got a flexible idea of 'fresh'.
The Guild hall's the one with the notice board. Read the small print, and if it says 'minor wolves', don't believe the 'minor'.
Sleep at the inn, not the barn. The barn's cheaper, but the goat has a grudge against travellers.
Keep your sword sheathed in the square. People here don't mind a stranger, but they mind one who looks busy.
The doctor's good, but the whole town will know your business by supper, so decide what you're ill with before you go in.
Stay out of the fields at sundown. That's when the wolves come up to see what's been planted.
Say good morning to everyone, and I mean everyone. We've got people here who've been offended since before you were born.
Best meal in town is at the priest's house, and all it costs is listening to him for an hour.
Don't hit anyone where the guards can see you, and don't hit anyone where the old women can see you. The guards are the kinder of the two.
Ask for #food# at the inn, and don't ask what's in it. #saying#
If a farmer tells you #small_trouble#, that isn't small talk, it's an offer of work. Walk on, or roll up your sleeves.
Tell them {me} sent you. They'll charge you more, but they'll be polite about it.
place:city: Keep your purse at the front, your hand on it, and your eyes on anyone being friendly.
Never draw steel inside the walls. The watch is one thing, but the golems don't take bribes.
The Guild's on the main road, and the market's wherever it gets loud. Anything sold to you in a side street fell off a cart, or a person.
First price is an insult. You're expected to insult them back. It's how people here say hello.
If someone in a nice coat offers to show you around, they're going to show you to the door of their cousin's shop.
Don't stare at the keep for too long. The guards have nothing else to do, and they've started keeping a list.
The inn by the gate charges double for the view of the gate. Walk one more street and sleep for half.
You can get anything in this city, {you}. That's not a boast, it's a warning.
There's a lot of law here and not much justice, so stay out of the first and you won't need the second.
If you get lost, follow the smell of bread to the market or the smell of fish to the docks. If it smells of neither, turn round.
Be polite to the clerks. A knight can only kill you, but a clerk can lose your paperwork.
#saying# They've got that on a sign in {home}, over the debtors' prison.
If you want #food# that won't kill you, ask a guard where they eat. Ask a lawyer where they don't.
place:elf: Speak softly, and don't pick anything, not even if it's on the ground. It may be resting.
If an elder stops in the middle of a sentence, wait. They may well be back by evening.
Never cut a living branch here. I saw what happened to the last man who did. It was a long time ago, and his descendants are still apologising.
Don't tell anyone how young they look. You'd be surprised what offends us.
We don't have an inn so much as a willingness to let you lie down. Say thank you to the hammock.
The rangers know you're here. They've known for two days. Waving is unnecessary, but appreciated.
Bring your own food, unless you're fond of leaves. We're very proud of the leaves.
The herbalist will heal you if you ask nicely. She'll also tell you what you're doing wrong with your life, free of charge.
Don't ask how old anything is. You'll be told, at length, with dates.
Mind your boots on the moss. That patch has been growing since before your kingdom had a name.
Nothing here is locked, and nothing has ever been stolen. I'd like you to think about why that might be.
#saying# Humans say that a lot. Here, try saying nothing. It's very popular.
place:elfcity: Bow at the third landing, not the second. The second is for people who've given up.
You'll be kept waiting. That isn't an insult. It's how you know you're being taken seriously.
The bridges sway. They're meant to. Looking down is not recommended, even by the ones who grew them.
Never interrupt a song, however long it goes on. Especially if it's long. It's usually about someone's family.
If you want to see {elf_title} {elf_ruler}, start asking now. With luck, your grandchildren will be received.
Everyone at court is being polite to you, {you}. I'd start to worry, if I were you.
The Elder Tree is not a landmark. It's a resident. Don't lean on it.
Say less than you mean and mean less than you say, and you may get through dinner.
The merchants here don't haggle. They look at you sadly until you've paid.
Wear something clean. You won't look like one of us, but we'll see that you tried.
Everything up here is higher than it looks. If you fall, try to do it quietly. There's a recital.
If you've brought #food#, keep it in your pack. The smell alone would be a diplomatic incident.
place:beast: Eat what you're offered, all of it, and ask for more. Turning down food is how you start a feud.
If someone slaps you on the back and you fall over, get up laughing. That's the whole test.
Say it straight, whatever it is. We can smell a lie, and it smells like city.
Don't walk past the chief's fire without saying hello. Loudly. We can't hear polite here.
Someone's going to ask you to wrestle, {you}. Say yes. Lose well. You'll have friends for life.
Keep to the fires after dark. The orcs come down onto the grass, and the grass won't warn you twice.
Never step over a sleeping hunter. Go round. There's a reason so few people have tried it.
Your money's no good here. Well, it is, but a story and a strong arm will get you a better deal.
If you're going south, tell someone first. Past the last fires, nobody comes looking.
